data.title: Suspicious "final demand before seizure" from EuroClaim (Cyprus)
data.summary: EuroClaim Forderungsmanagement Ltd. (Limassol, Cyprus) dated 3 August 2026 demands €287.40 for an alleged phone-signed prize-draw subscription "Lotto-Muster-Club". It demands payment within 72 hours, by 6 August 2026, to a Lithuanian IBAN held by a private individual.
data.explanation: This letter has several typical scam or aggressive dubious-collection features: a 72-hour deadline, threats of account seizure, a negative SCHUFA entry and criminal charges, payment to a Lithuanian account in a private person's name, and the claim that objecting is pointless. Real collection agencies must name the original creditor and contract, and they don't pay into private accounts. Do not pay right away. Check whether you ever had such a subscription. If not, ask the sender in writing for proof of the claim. You could also contact a consumer advice centre (Verbraucherzentrale) or a lawyer, and consider reporting it to the police. A collection letter alone does not allow seizure of your account. Only a court title could lead to that.

warnings: Payment is demanded within 72 hours to a Lithuanian IBAN held by a private individual, which is a strong scam indicator.
The letter threatens account seizure, SCHUFA entry and criminal charges and says objecting is pointless, which is pressure tactics.
The letter does not name the contract date or the creditor's address, and it uses a generic salutation.
Fees of €84.00 and €24.00 are unexplained and may be unlawful.
Do not pay or call the number before checking the claim independently.
